compare.intro: To tell the ten apart, look at what sits next to the blank: between two nouns you need の or と, after the topic you need は or も, before a noun この (これ stands alone), and at the very end です, じゃありません, か, ね or よ.

forms.tag: ちがう・おなじ · topic or "too"
forms.ja: [今日|きょう]{は}[休|やす]みです。あした{も}[休|やす]みです。
forms.en: Today is a day off. Tomorrow is a day off too.

forms.tag: ひとりで・＋もの · alone or + noun
forms.ja: {これ}はわたしのペンです。{この}ペンは[安|やす]いです。
forms.en: This is my pen. This pen is cheap.

forms.tag: どんな・AとB · of or and
forms.ja: これは[日本語|にほんご]{の}[本|ほん]{と}ノートです。
forms.en: These are a Japanese book and a notebook.

check.label: がっこうで
check.q: A：この[白|しろ]いノートは^だれの^ですか。B：[先生|せんせい]（　　）です。
why: 先生とです would mean "with the teacher". A asked whose notebook it is.
A asks だれの, "whose". 先生のです answers it: it is the teacher's.
先生もです would mean "the teacher too". It does not say whose the notebook is.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: [今週|こんしゅう]は[休|やす]みです。^[来週|らいしゅう]^（　　）^[休|やす]みです^。
why: と joins two nouns, as in 今週と来週は休みです. Here 来週 stands alone before 休みです, so と has nothing to join.
来週か休みです is not a sentence. A question か goes at the very end, after です.
This week is a day off, and next week is the same, so も: "next week too".
を marks the thing an action is done to. 休みです is not an action.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^[先週|せんしゅう]^（　　）テストはどれですか。
why: この points at a thing near you. It cannot come right after 先週.
先週のテスト is "last week's test": の joins the two nouns.
と means "and". 先週とテスト would be "last week and the test".
これ stands alone and never comes before a noun. 先週これテスト is not Japanese.

drill.label: Choose the ending
drill.q: （^ふたりでカレンダーを[見|み]ています^。）A「わあ、[毎日|まいにち]クラスがあります（　　）。」B「^ほんとうですね^。」
why: よ tells news the other person does not know. B is looking at the same calendar.
Both can see the calendar, so A shares what they both see: ね. B agrees.
か asks. A can see the answer, and B replies by agreeing, not answering.
を marks the thing an action is done to. It cannot end a sentence.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^[父|ちち]は[先生|せんせい]です^。[母|はは]^も^[先生|せんせい]（　　）。
why: も says the mother is the same as the father. He is a teacher, so she is a teacher too: 先生です.
This would say she is not a teacher. That does not match も after "father is a teacher".
ます goes after a verb. 先生 is a noun.
を marks the thing an action is done to. The sentence would have no ending.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: この is followed by a noun. Which tile is a noun?
drill.full: すみません、{この}クラスは[何時|なんじ]からですか。
drill.explain: この needs a noun right after it, and クラスは is the topic. Then 何時から asks the start time, and ですか closes the question.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: A「[午後|ごご]もクラスがありますか。」B「はい、
tiles: [中山|なかやま][先生|せんせい]の
drill.hint: Start with the topic. Whose class is it?
drill.full: A「[午後|ごご]もクラスがありますか。」B「はい、[午後|ごご]は[中山|なかやま][先生|せんせい]{の}クラスですよ。」
drill.explain: 午後は is the topic, so it comes first. 中山先生の tells whose class, so it sits right before クラス. です closes the sentence, and よ after it tells A something new.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: マリアさん（　　）　トムさんは　この　学校の　学生です。
exam.explain: と joins two people: マリアさんとトムさん are both students here. の would make Tom "Maria's Tom", which makes no sense. マリアさんも　トムさんは does not work: for both you would need マリアさんも　トムさんも. を marks the thing an action is done to.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q:
A「あしたは　休みですか。」
B「いいえ、あしたも　クラスが　あります（　　）。」
exam.explain: A did not know and asked, so B tells new information: よ. ね is for something both people already know, but A just asked. か would turn B's answer into a question, and を cannot end a sentence.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.before: A「これは　あなたの　かさですか。」B「いいえ、
exam.full: A「これは　あなたの　かさですか。」B「いいえ、それはわたしのかさ{じゃありません}。友だちのです。」
exam.explain: それは, わたしの, かさ, じゃありません. それは is the topic: the umbrella is near A, so B says それ. わたしの goes before かさ, and じゃありません comes last, after the noun.

scene.ja: 日本語学校のカレンダー
scene.en: The week's calendar at a language school
scene.intro: Tap each word on the calendar by the front door of your language school.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: あしたの　_ごご_は　テストが　あります。
check.explain: ごご is 午後: 午 (noon) and 後 (after). 午前 is ごぜん, the morning. 五後 uses 五, the number five, not 午. 後午 has the two kanji the wrong way round.

skill.ask: Which line of the notice holds the one fact you need?
skill.passage:
さくら日本語学校
今週の　かいわの　クラス
十二日（月）　午後　二時〜三時
十三日（火）　^午前^　十時〜十一時
十五日（木）　午後　二時〜三時
^十六日（金）　午前^　十時〜十一時
※　^十三日は　先生が　休みです。クラスは　ありません。^
skill.strategy: Read the question first, then look only at the lines with 午前, and check the note at the bottom.

item.q: リンさんは　午前の　かいわの　クラスに　出たいです。何日に　学校へ　行きますか。
item.explain: Only two lines say 午前: the 13th and the 16th. The note says the teacher is off on the 13th and there is no class, so Lin goes on the 16th.
why: The class on the 12th is 午後, in the afternoon.
The 13th has a morning class, but the note says the teacher is off and there is no class.
The class on the 15th is 午後, in the afternoon.
